title: SIPPO — a bubble tea brand with a pixel smile
seo_title: SIPPO Bubble Tea Brand Identity | Muhammad Babar
description: Brand identity case study for SIPPO bubble tea: a pixel wordmark, a mascot with three moods, a lime and pink palette, and packaging, merch and a shopfront.
summary: A playful identity for a bubble tea brand: a pixel wordmark, a mascot with three moods and a loud lime and pink palette, carried from cup sleeves to the shopfront.
cover_alt: SIPPO pixel wordmark in black with the waving pink mascot on an acid lime background

sections.label: The idea
sections.heading: Bubble tea that doesn’t take itself too seriously
sections.body:
SIPPO is a bubble tea brand made for a young, social crowd. The identity leans into fun: a chunky pixel wordmark that reads like a game title, a cheeky mascot, and two loud colours set against black and a warm off-white.

The aim was a small system that is simple enough to print on a cup sleeve and strong enough to carry a whole shopfront.

sections.label: Wordmark
sections.heading: A pixel wordmark that reads like a game title
sections.body:
SIPPO is drawn on a square pixel grid, with stepped curves on the S and a slanted O that gives the name a little movement. The heavy strokes stay readable when the logo is small on a cup and still feel crisp metres wide on a window.

Small labels such as BUBBLE TEA are set in a widely spaced monospace that sits under the logo without competing with it.

sections.label: Colour
sections.heading: Two loud colours, two quiet ones
sections.body: Lime and pink do the shouting. Ink black carries the wordmark and type, and a warm off-white gives the mascot drawings room to breathe.

sections.label: Mascot & touchpoints
sections.heading: One character, everywhere the brand goes
sections.body:
The mascot is a round pixel character drawn on the same grid as the wordmark, in three moods: a wave hello, a wink, and a cool pose with sunglasses and a lime burst. Each works on its own, so it can sit on a cup, a T-shirt or a window without the logo next to it.

The same few pieces carry the brand across cup sleeves that alternate lime and pink, a pink two-cup carrier, black and white T-shirts, a pink hanging sign and a lime window graphic.
